study.title: Acupuncture Decreases Blood Pressure Related to Hypothalamus Functional Connectivity with Frontal Lobe, Cerebellum, and Insula: A Study of Instantaneous and Short-Term Acupuncture Treatment in Essential Hypertension
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial; complete randomized block design; two parallel arms; resting-state fMRI before and after acupuncture interventions
study.blinding: Participants' eyes were masked with eyeshades and earplugs worn; blinding of assessors or practitioners not explicitly stated
study.population: Essential hypertension patients recruited from different community hospitals in Guangzhou; age 45–65 years; right-handed
study.disease_condition: Essential hypertension (mild or moderate arterial hypertension, grade 1 or 2)
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) mild or moderate arterial hypertension, grade 1 or 2 of the European Society of Hypertension-European Society of Cardiology Guidelines 2003, with the use of antihypertensive drugs but with a clear history of hypertension, with species and dose of antihypertensive medicine not being changed during the study period; (2) age between 45 and 65 years and right handedness; (3) regular diet with minimal liquor, tobacco, tea, and coffee consumption and normal sleeping patterns (before 12 a.m.); moderate-sized body mass index of 18.5–23.9 (Chinese); no history of nervous system disease; (4) no pain (including dysmenorrhea) or insomnia within 1 month before the test; (5) no metallic substances in the body, such as stents; (6) no noise exposure and hypothermia; no fear of confined spaces; (7) no acupuncture procedure within 1 month before the test
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) hypertensive crisis or other emergency; (2) inability to follow this study because of personal reasons

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: on the dorsum of the foot, in the depression anterior to the junction of the first and second metatarsal bones (Chinese National Standards GB/T12346)
interventions.needle_type_exact: Huatuo acupuncture needles, Suzhou, China; sterile
interventions.manipulation_exact: After developing needle sensation, twirling at an angle of 90–180° and a frequency of 60–90 times/min and lifting and thrusting at a range of 0.3–0.5 cm and a frequency of 60–90 times/min were conducted. After manipulating the needle for 1 min, the needle was held in place for 30 min. During the 30 min, the physician repeated this manipulation for 1 min every 10 min.
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Subjects were asked to pass urine and stool prior to treatment. The patients' eyes were masked with eyeshades, and earplugs were simultaneously worn so that their audiovisual system could not be stimulated.

extraction_notes.note: The sham group SF-36 scores after treatment appear to duplicate the LR3 group post-treatment values for RP, BP, GH, VI, SF, RE, and MH in the text (page 5). This appears to be a transcription error in the original paper. Values reported as sham group post-treatment are identical to LR3 post-treatment values in the first passage. A second set of sham baseline values is then reported. Extracted values are copied verbatim as reported.
No adverse events are reported in the paper. The paper does not explicitly state that no adverse events occurred.

No formal deqi measurement instrument (e.g., MASS, Deqi Scale) is reported. The paper only states 'after developing needle sensation' as part of the intervention description. Quantitative deqi data are absent.
No formal blinding assessment or allocation guessing data are reported beyond the use of eyeshades and earplugs for participants. Practitioner blinding is not addressed.
STAI scores are not reported numerically. The instrument was administered but no values, group comparisons, or statistical tests for STAI are presented in the results.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 2, Methods section 2.2; Pages 4–5, Results section 3.1

extraction_notes.note: The paper does not explicitly state the coordinate space (MNI vs Talairach) used for neuroimaging coordinates. However, the preprocessing pipeline uses SPM8 with EPI template normalization and REST software, and the paper refers to 'corresponding MNI coordinate' in the statistical analysis section. MNI is recorded as coordinate_space_reported_exact for all coordinate entries.

The n_analyzed for neuroimaging is inferred as 14 per group based on the flow chart showing 14 completers per arm. The paper does not explicitly state the neuroimaging analysis sample size in the results tables.

No between-group neuroimaging comparisons (LR3 vs sham) are reported in the results tables, only within-group pre vs post contrasts. The discussion compares findings narratively but no direct between-group fMRI contrast table is provided.

No short-term treatment neuroimaging data for the sham group (pre vs post-treatment contrast for sham) is reported in the paper. Only pre vs post-once and pre vs post-treatment for LR3, and pre vs post-once for sham are presented.
The laterality of the LR3 acupoint used is not specified in the paper (bilateral or unilateral). This is a limitation for intervention replication.
Filtering parameters (bandpass filter range) for resting-state fMRI preprocessing are not reported in the methods.
Global signal regression status is not reported in the preprocessing description.

The statistical test used for blood pressure comparison is not specified (only 'paired t-test' is mentioned generically in Methods section 2.2.5 for within-group comparisons; the exact test for BP data is inferred from general methods).

Table 3 ROI 3 left hemisphere: the MNI coordinate -9 -15 51 results in a y-coordinate of -15 which is unusual for medial frontal gyrus. This is transcribed exactly as in the paper and may represent an error in the original publication.
No PMID is provided in the paper. DOI is extracted from the article header.
